title: Nimorith, the Gray Benefactor
subtitle: Absence & Threshold

lore.description:
Fae magic has two hands. The courts are famous for the one that gives — the glamour, the seeming, the face over the face, the gold that is leaves in the morning. Everything Mab is celebrated for is addition.

Nimorith is the other hand.

Trow work is **subtractive**. Not destruction, which is loud and leaves debris — removal. The mouth taken so that the speaking stops. The memory lifted out with the grammar closing over it. The name gone from a thing that still stands there wanting to be called something. A Trow does not defeat you. A Trow reaches into the situation and removes the part that was doing the work, and what is left is not damaged. It simply no longer includes that.

He does not arrive. He is the pause you eventually notice, and then cannot stop noticing, and then cannot remember the shape of afterward.
lore.followers: Those who bargain with him learn that presence is a luxury, absence a currency, and the space between doors a kingdom unto itself. To serve him is to walk at the corner of sight, to speak in the breath held before truth is told. His followers are spies, treaty-witnesses, archivists, and anyone who has learned that the most valuable thing in a negotiation is what was never written down.
lore.quote: Take what is not there and you shall have what never was. The gap is the gift; the missing, the mercy.
lore.what_is_taken_is_kept:
Nothing subtracted is annihilated. It is held, and holding is not free.

A Trow who has taken much is carrying much, and it shows. What is worn on the outside of an old Trow is not disguise and not glamour: it is the accumulated remainder of every bargain they could not unwind — faces off people who are still alive and no longer have them, voices, a particular way of laughing, the memory of a room. They wear these because there is nowhere else to put them. Ask one why it changes and you will be told, accurately, that these are faces it has worn, and you will take that for a figure of speech.
lore.the_price_of_a_large_subtraction:
Small takings cost little. A large one has to be sealed, and a seal must weigh what the subtraction weighs — which means that past a certain size, the only component a Trow has left of sufficient weight is its own name.

So the greatest subtractions are mutual. The one who lost it does not know what they lost. The one who took it does not know they took it. Both walk away intact, both walk away lighter, and there is no one left in the arrangement who could undo it even if asked, because asking would require a word that neither party still holds.
lore.a_worked_example:
Saikou Ira left a silver mirror at the Ninth Name Shrine. It shows a viewer not their own face but the face of the child they failed to protect, and it has nine cracks, and the ninth weeps. Exorcists travel a long way to look into it and most of them will not talk about it afterward.

Saikou looked into it. He did not recognize the face.

He has said, on the record, that he knows he has forgotten a daughter — her name and her face both — and that he does not know why or when, and that the not-knowing-why is worse than the loss. He has spent decades on it. He is the most methodical man of his generation and he keeps complete accounts of every exorcism he has performed, and the accounts run to eighteen, and there are seventeen of them.

That gap is the whole of the evidence, and it is conclusive to anyone who knows the trade. A demon that takes a memory never takes the memory of the exorcism — it wants the exorcist to know it won. The seventeenth is not missing because something ate it. It is missing because something *removed* it, cleanly, along with everything the removal would otherwise have been noticed by.

There is a figure who walks the old roads in gray and has been on them a long time, and they are not what they are generally taken for. They do not remember the arrangement either. They paid the seal with the only thing heavy enough — it was theirs, and it is gone — and what is gone is the part that would have answered to anything. People reach for a pronoun with them and find that none of the available ones catch, and settle on *they* not out of courtesy but because it is accurate: there is no one in there to be a him. They go on changing faces and cannot say why they have so many. Somewhere in what they are carrying is a girl's face that means nothing to them and would mean everything to a man they have never, to their knowledge, met.

**For the GM:** the players may assemble this. No character in the setting can. Do not let an NPC arrive at it, do not let a divination return it, and never let the two of them recognize each other. The pieces are all placed and they are meant to stay placed.
lore.on_the_trow_and_identity:
Trow read as masculine to most people who meet one, and most Trow will let that stand because correcting it would require caring. It is not accurate. A Trow's selfhood is the first thing its own craft erodes: every subtraction is carried, and a carrier who has taken enough is largely composed of other people's material.

The old ones are therefore *they*, and it is not a courtesy. It is a count. There is not one of anything in there to point at, and the ones who have spent their names have not even got the thing a name would have been attached to.

domain_focus: Thresholds & Liminality: doors, gates, moments of transition, the unseen
Absence & Omission: erasure, forgetting, silence, what is not said
Memory & Witness: testimony, collateral, the price of truth
Subtlety & Misdirection: stealth, deception by omission, unseen paths

thiasos.description: Nimorith does not ask a Runekeeper to bind a familiar of flesh and blood. Their Thiasos is a creature of silence and gaps: a moth that flies only in the blind spot of the eye, a spider that weaves webs only in unlit corners, a mouse that is only ever heard, never seen, or a patch of shadow that moves against the light.
thiasos.care: This creature requires no food, but it must be offered a silence daily — a minute of absolute stillness and quiet contemplation from its bearer. If neglected for a week, it becomes Compromised (it fades, imposing –1 die on all Stealth or Subterfuge rolls for its bearer until a significant silence is given).

codex.description: Nimorith's Codex is never a whole book. It may be a collection of blank vellum pages that reveal writing only when held in a specific type of shadow, a slate that must be dusted with ash from an extinguished lamp, or a key that unlocks a non-existent drawer.
codex.upkeep: Because Nimorith's truths are written in omissions, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week in a truly liminal space (a doorway at twilight, a forgotten attic, a crossroads) and erase one of their own memories onto its pages, or the symbols fade (treat as Compromised until a suitable omission is made).

patrons_gift.name: Nimorith's Absence
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Nimorith may focus on a specific absence — a missing object, a silent moment, an unlit lamp.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, they gain +1 die to Stealth or Subterfuge rolls that exploit that absence, and the first time each scene they would fail to move unseen through a threshold, they may reroll the check (the shadows part for them).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Nimorith.

rites.name: The Unmeasured Room
rites.materials: An inward-opening door; a held breath to the count of three.
rites.effect: Create one Gap token — a specific absence that others ignore (a watcher forgets a latch, a ledger skips a line, a patrol overlooks a side door). You gain +1 die when exploiting this gap. An ally may spend 1 Boon to treat one failed roll as 'never happened' (retcon of that action only).
rites.push_it: The gap becomes contagious: nearby like-absences echo. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Borrowed Memory
rites.materials: A silver thread tied fingertip-to-fingertip; a whispered 'I was there.'
rites.effect: Hold another's specific memory as collateral. Gain +1 die on actions grounded in that memory's context. Memory returns slightly out of order unless 'paid in full' with a truthful account before witnesses.
rites.push_it: Hold two memories simultaneously; mark +1 Obligation as temporal dissonance builds. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: The Missing Line
rites.materials: A document with space for amendment; a shadowless gray feather.
rites.effect: Cause one clause, name, or line to vanish from a witnessed text. DV = complexity/scope. On success, the erasure is seamless and socially 'always so.'
rites.push_it: The omission propagates to directly-referenced copies; mark +1 SB (Diamonds) as reality adjusts. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Duskmark's Passage
rites.materials: Two duskmarks set at twilight; an unlit pipe that smokes by itself.
rites.effect: Declare safe-conduct between the paired thresholds. Allies gain +2 dice to Traverse; enemies suffer -1 die to intercept within the lane. A counter-witness at either end can block.
rites.push_it: Passage becomes bidirectional for the scene; mark +1 Obligation — the path remembers you. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Veil-Bending
rites.materials: A room with four doors; a mirror that reflects only doorways.
rites.effect: Reverse directions within the space; quiet a name until dawn; align exits with intent rather than map. Zone gains the [VEIL] tag: +2 dice to misdirection; -2 dice to direct confrontation.
rites.push_it: Make it permanent for this site; start Threshold Drift [6] as the place migrates from the world. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Nimorith does not sing notes, but the spaces between notes. Their music is one of rests, pauses, and breaths held too long. Their voice is used to erase sound, to make a crowded room feel empty, or to make a promise forgotten before it is fully heard. Nimorith's Cantors are often found in places of negotiation or treaty-signing, ensuring the final agreement contains the necessary, profitable omissions.

cult.name: The Cult of the Absent Host
cult.description: Nimorith's cults gather in non-places: abandoned train stations at midnight, the attics of forgotten houses, the space under a bridge that no one claims. The Absent Host is a fellowship of those who profit from what is not said and what is not seen. A ritual of the Cult involves a shared meal where one seat is always left empty for Nimorith, and the most valuable dish is the one that is never served. Their creed is written in smoke and fading light: 'The greatest gift is an exit no one remembers. The greatest truth is the one left unspoken.' Outsiders are welcome if they bring a secret to erase.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Threshold-Weaver
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with Nimorith is a threshold-weaver or gap-monger — one who crafts with absence and silence. Their magic works through the materials of negation: a candle that burns darkness instead of light, a key that opens locks by making them forget they are locked, or a scissor that cuts the threads of memory. Their tools are never whole; they use broken mirrors, half-spoken words, and borrowed shadows.
witchcraft.lore: The gap-monger's path is patience with the unwritten. They learn that the most complete document is the one with a single line missing, that the safest room is the one no one remembers entering, and that a debt owed for a secret erased is a debt that can never quite be collected — because no one can prove it was ever there.
witchcraft.quote: The greatest gift is an exit no one remembers.

duskmark_lantern.name: The Duskmark Lantern
duskmark_lantern.description: A lantern with panes of smoked glass that seems to absorb light rather than cast it. Once per session, the witch may light this lantern (though it produces no visible flame) in a doorway or threshold. For the next scene, the threshold becomes veiled; those who pass through it are not immediately noticed, and sounds are dampened. The lantern grows cold when it is ready to be used again.

hedge_gifts.name: Whisper of Omission
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may whisper a single word into someone's ear. That word is temporarily erased from the target's vocabulary; they cannot speak it or understand it for the next hour. This can be used to disable a command word, prevent a warning, or simply cause profound confusion.

hedge_gifts.name: Gap in the Ledger
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, touch a written record (a logbook, a guest list, a manifest) and cause a single entry to be skipped when next read aloud or copied. The original entry is not destroyed, merely overlooked, until someone specifically searches for it.

hedge_gifts.name: Held Breath
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, for one exchange, you and everyone within Near of you become momentarily unremarkable — witnesses who glance your way retain no specific detail of what they saw, though they know something happened.

monastic_tradition.name: Threshold Warden
monastic_tradition.description: You do not guard the door; you guard the idea of the door. You watch the unwatched space.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Wits 3+, Stealth 2+, Rite of the Unmeasured Room or Cantor of Nimorith.
monastic_tradition.quote: The gap is the gift; the missing, the mercy.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: Monks of the Threshold Warden understand that a promise is just another threshold. They gain +1 die to resist any debt or obligation that would bind them to a specific location or compel them to speak plain truth. If they succeed, the obligation's wording temporarily blurs, as if the ink had run.

basic.name: Unseen Path
basic.description: Once per scene, you may step from one shadow to another within Near, provided neither is under direct observation.

advanced.name: Erase the Moment
advanced.description: When you would be noticed, you may spend a Boon to have the observer simply overlook you, as if your presence was a trick of the light.

master.name: Keeper of the Unlit Pipe
master.description: Once per session, you can enforce a profound silence upon a Zone. For one scene, all sound ceases, all lights gutter out, and all witnesses find their attention sliding away from the area. Those within gain +2 dice to Stealth and Subterfuge. After using this talent, you mark +1 permanent Corruption (your own outline becomes faint) and +1 Obligation to Nimorith — a silence this deep always demands a reciprocal noise eventually.
master.cost: 1 permanent Corruption and +1 Obligation to Nimorith

corruption.benefit: Shadow-Step: Once/scene, move between witnessed thresholds in Near.
corruption.cost: Almost-Presence: In crowds you slip notice; begin Position –1 when trying to stand out.

corruption.benefit: Gap-Sense: +1 die to Notice when something vital is missing or altered.
corruption.cost: Blind Spot: You may miss the obvious present while hunting absences.

corruption.benefit: Echo-Accounting: Once/session, ensure a vow 'takes' by finding its last true witness.
corruption.cost: Witness Weight: Maintain three active witness tokens or suffer –1 die to social rolls.

corruption.benefit: Flow-Nudge: Once/scene, open the exit you meant; close the boastful boast.
corruption.cost: Direction Drift: Maps resist you; –1 die to Navigation without a living guide.

corruption.benefit: Absence Artisan: Once/session, create a beneficial absence (forgotten debt, skipped patrol, missing line).
corruption.cost: Obligation Void: Others forget promises owed to you; –1 die to enforce agreements.

corruption.benefit: Gray Dominion: Once/session, declare an area 'properly absent': allies +2 dice to stealth/deception; foes –2 dice to detection/truth.
corruption.cost: Reality Thinning: Mark +2 Obligation; risk permanent Harm from existing half-out-of-world.

playstyle_notes.description:
Nimorith is for a player who wants power that removes rather than adds, and who can accept that the cost is paid in things they will not be able to miss accurately. His gifts do not blast, charm, or conceal — they excise. A guard who no longer has the concept of the door he is guarding. A creditor who retains the debt and has lost your face. A room that is one room shorter than it was.

Run his intrusions as absences the player notices sideways: an ally who cannot say a particular word any more and has not registered it, a name everyone at the table has stopped using, a scene that clearly had a fourth person in it. Never announce a subtraction. The correct player experience is realizing, two sessions late, that something has been gone for a while.
emphasizes: Subtraction, not destruction — the thing removed, the situation intact around the hole
Nothing annihilated — what is taken is carried by whoever took it, and shows
Mutual forgetting — the largest workings cost the caster their own name to seal
Absence noticed late — the table should discover a loss rather than witness one
The gap as evidence — what is missing is the only reliable testimony

sample_adventure.title: The Peace That Was Never Signed
sample_adventure.description: Two rival houses believe a treaty was signed at their last parley, ending a blood feud. Neither house's copy of the document exists — nor does anyone quite remember the signing, only the relief that followed. Someone is unmaking the peace one omission at a time, and unless the party can find the last true witness to that room, the feud will resume as if the years of quiet had never happened. Nimorith is watching to see if they value the peace enough to pay its price twice.
sample_adventure.quote: You do not need to remember the treaty to keep it. You only need to stop noticing that you have forgotten it was ever broken.
